messages:
mona: FYI seeing a sudden spike in conntrack drops on eu-south1 gpufleet, some model-serving pods losing east-west connections.
opsbot: [alert] conntrack table 98% full on host gpu-node-07 (nf_conntrack=65536)
samir: link? logs?
mona: logs attached — tail from node:
```
[2026-11-02T10:03:41Z] nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet.
[2026-11-02T10:03:42Z] TCP: request_sock_TCP: Possible SYN flooding on port 31000. Sending cookies.
```
jorge: are we seeing ephemeral port exhaustion too or just conntrack? run `ss -tan src :31000` and `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max`
elaine: ran quick check: nf_conntrack_max=65536, fd usage fine, ephemeral ports ~50k used across nodes — but many short-lived SYN_RECV entries from model-prefetch pods
samir: sounds like prefetch fanout + small MTU/RDMA retransmits causing handshake retries -> conntrack churn. Reduce prefetch concurrency and increase conntrack_max on hot nodes.
mona: temp mitigations I've pushed: scale down prefetch replicas on eu-south1 by 30%, applied `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` on gpupool nodes for now. Monitoring.
opsbot: deploy 1956f3 by @mona to eu-south1-preemptible completed :white_check_mark:
jorge: long term: we should implement per-daemonset conntrack isolation (conntrack namespace) or use SNAT pool expansion + source NAT affinity. Also add readiness backoff on model prefetch.
elaine: +1. Also propose updating kube-proxy conntrack settings and adding a egress NAT gateway to reduce SNAT churn. I'll put a runbook PR.
mona: thanks — keeping this thread open. If drops persist beyond 30m I'll start rolling kernel-level tuning across region and open a support ticket with cloud provider for DNAT table metrics.
samir: ping me if you need to revert the nf_conntrack change. :thumbsup:
